translated.evidence: We select a subset of the following two NER tasks, CoNLL-2002 NER (Sang, 2002) and CoNLL-2003 NER (Sang and De Meulder, 2003). CoNLL NER datasets are natively annotated in each language from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: The XGLUE paper reuses CoNLL-2002/2003 NER and does not provide details about the original annotators. The original CoNLL shared tasks used annotators but demographics are not described here.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Source data is from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, which contains natively created text in each language, not translated content.

CoNLL NER.annotation_quality_notes: Existing dataset from CoNLL-2002 and CoNLL-2003 shared tasks. 4 entity types: Person, Location, Organization, Miscellaneous. F1 metric.

translated.evidence: Subset of Universal Dependencies (UD) Treebanks (v2.5), which are natively constructed treebanks for each language.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: The XGLUE paper does not discuss the annotators of the UD Treebanks. UD Treebanks are typically created by language experts, but this is not stated in this paper.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Universal Dependencies Treebanks contain native-language text for each language.

UDPOS.annotation_quality_notes: Existing dataset from UD Treebanks v2.5. ACC metric.

translated.evidence: We crawl this dataset from Microsoft News (MSN). News articles are natively written in each language on the MSN platform.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: Labels are category labels from the MSN website, reviewed by human, but the paper does not state whether the reviewers are native speakers of each language.

culturally_grounded.evidence: News articles are crawled from MSN in each language, representing region-specific news content.

NC.annotation_quality_notes: New dataset created by this paper. 10 news categories. Category labels from MSN website, human-reviewed. ACC metric.

translated.evidence: The MLQA is a multilingual machine reading comprehension task, which contains QA annotations labeled in 7 languages. MLQA annotations are natively created in each language based on Wikipedia articles.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: The XGLUE paper does not describe the MLQA annotator demographics. This information would be in the original MLQA paper (Lewis et al., 2019b).

culturally_grounded.evidence: MLQA uses parallel Wikipedia passages across languages, so while QA pairs are created natively, the underlying content is parallel/shared across languages rather than culturally specific.

MLQA.annotation_quality_notes: Existing dataset. F1 metric. Data sourced from Wikipedia.

translated.evidence: We reuse the original XNLI dataset (Conneau et al., 2018) in XGLUE. XNLI is a translation of the MultiNLI English corpus into 14 other languages.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: The XGLUE paper does not describe the XNLI translators. The original XNLI paper used professional translators.

culturally_grounded.evidence: XNLI is translated from English MultiNLI corpus, inheriting English-centric content and cultural assumptions.

XNLI.annotation_quality_notes: Existing translated dataset. ACC metric. Translated from English MultiNLI to 14 other languages.

translated.evidence: The PAWS-X (Yang et al., 2019a) is a paraphrase identification dataset, which extends the Wikipedia portion of the PAWS (Zhang et al., 2019) evaluation to more languages. PAWS-X translates English PAWS pairs into other languages.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: The XGLUE paper does not describe the PAWS-X translation process or annotators.

culturally_grounded.evidence: PAWS-X extends English Wikipedia PAWS data to other languages via translation, inheriting English-centric content.

PAWS-X.annotation_quality_notes: Existing translated dataset. ACC metric. XGLUE uses a 4-language subset (en, es, fr, de) of the original PAWS-X.

translated.evidence: We construct this dataset based on Bing. Queries and ads are natively sourced from Bing search in each language.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: Labeled on a Microsoft internal crowdsourcing platform with guidelines and testing, but whether labelers are native speakers of each language is not stated.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Data is natively sourced from Bing search queries and ads in each language, reflecting real user search behavior.

QADSM.annotation_quality_notes: New dataset. 3 annotators per sample, majority vote. Labelers passed a training guideline and labeling test. Binary classification. ACC metric.

translated.evidence: We construct this dataset based on Bing. Queries and web pages are natively sourced from Bing search in each language.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: Labeled on a Microsoft internal crowdsourcing platform with guidelines and testing, but whether labelers are native speakers of each language is not stated.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Data is natively sourced from Bing search queries and web pages in each language.

WPR.annotation_quality_notes: New dataset. 3 annotators per sample, majority vote. Labelers passed a training guideline and labeling test. 5-level relevance rating. nDCG metric.

translated.evidence: We construct this dataset based on Bing. Question-passage pairs are natively sourced from Bing in each language.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: Labeled on a Microsoft internal crowdsourcing platform with guidelines and testing, but whether labelers are native speakers of each language is not stated.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Data is natively sourced from Bing question-passage pairs in each language.

QAM.annotation_quality_notes: New dataset. 3 annotators per sample, majority vote. Labelers passed a training guideline and labeling test. Binary classification. ACC metric.

translated.evidence: We collect <passage, question> pairs from Bing. Data is natively sourced from Bing in each language.

native_annotators.evidence: All these 6 new tasks with * are labeled by human, except es, it and pt datasets in QG (80+% accuracy) are obtained by an in-house QA ranker. So en/fr/de have human annotation, while es/it/pt have automated labels.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Data is natively sourced from Bing passage-question pairs in each language.

QG.annotation_quality_notes: New dataset. en/fr/de labeled by human annotators (3 per sample, majority vote). es/it/pt labeled by in-house QA ranker with 80+% accuracy. BLEU-4 metric.

translated.evidence: We collect <news body, news title> pairs from Microsoft News (MSN). News titles and bodies are natively written in each language.

native_annotators.evidence: News titles are created by news publishers/editors natively in each language. Category labels from MSN are reviewed by human.

culturally_grounded.evidence: News body-title pairs are natively sourced from MSN in each language, representing region-specific news content.

NTG.annotation_quality_notes: New dataset. News body-title pairs from MSN. BLEU-4 metric. Training set only in English (300K instances).
